\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{काम} (kām)}{काम (kām)}]{\mw{काम} (kām) — work}

\label{lesson:MW-C167-kam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for to lie down, then the Marwadi for dusk.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{काम}}
\textbf{\mw{काम}} — \emph{kām} — \textquotedblleft{}work\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{हूं} \mw{रोज} \mw{घणो} \mw{काम} \mw{करूं} \mw{हूं।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hū̃ roj ghaṇo kām karū̃ hū̃.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I do a lot of work every day.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{काम}} (\emph{kām}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{karman}, \textquotedblleft{}act, work\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Marwari \emph{kām} (CDIAL 2892). With \textbf{\mw{करणो}} it is to work: \textbf{\mw{काम} \mw{करो}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what you do.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kām}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kām}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hū̃ roj ghaṇo kām karū̃ hū̃.} — I do a lot of work every day.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for to lie down, then the Marwadi for dusk, then say \emph{kām} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \mw{काम} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Work\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{पैलो} (pailo)}{पैलो (pailo)}]{\mw{पैलो} (pailo) — first}

\label{lesson:MW-C167-pailo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for dusk, then the Marwadi for work.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{पैलो}}
\textbf{\mw{पैलो}} — \emph{pailo} — \textquotedblleft{}first\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{पैलो} \mw{काम} \mw{घणो} \mw{दोरो} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pailo kām ghaṇo doro hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The first job is very hard.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{पैलो}} (\emph{pailo}) is inherited from a reconstructed \emph{*prathila}, \textquotedblleft{}first\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Old Marwari \emph{pahalo} (CDIAL 8652). It agrees like an adjective: \textbf{\mw{पैली} \mw{रोटी}}, the first roti.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what you do.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{छांटणो} (chhā̃ṭṇo)}{छांटणो (chhā̃ṭṇo)}]{\mw{छांटणो} (chhā̃ṭṇo) — to sprinkle}

\label{lesson:MW-C167-chhatno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for work, then the Marwadi for first.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{छांटणो}}
\textbf{\mw{छांटणो}} — \emph{chhā̃ṭṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to sprinkle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{दिनूगै} \mw{मां} \mw{पाणी} \mw{छांटै} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dinūgai mā̃ pāṇī chhā̃ṭai hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Early in the morning my mother sprinkles water.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \mw{म्हैं} \mw{पाणी} \mw{छांट्यो}, \emph{mhaĩ pāṇī chhā̃ṭyo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{छांटणो}} (\emph{chhā̃ṭṇo}) comes from a reconstructed \emph{*chaṇṭ}, \textquotedblleft{}scatter\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Gujarati \emph{chā̃ṭvũ}, \textquotedblleft{}to sprinkle\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 4970). CDIAL gives no Marwari form in this entry.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for saying what you do.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{छेलो} (chhelo)}{छेलो (chhelo)}]{\mw{छेलो} (chhelo) — last}

\label{lesson:MW-C167-chhelo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for first, then the Marwadi for to sprinkle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{छेलो}}
\textbf{\mw{छेलो}} — \emph{chhelo} — \textquotedblleft{}last\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{छेलो} \mw{काम} \mw{सोरो} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{chhelo kām soro hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The last job is easy.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{छेलो}} (\emph{chhelo}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{cheda}, \textquotedblleft{}a piece cut off; a stopping\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Old Marwari \emph{chehalaü}, \textquotedblleft{}last, final\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 5064). It agrees like \textbf{\mw{पैलो}}: \textbf{\mw{छेली} \mw{बात}}, the last thing.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what you do.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{झट} (jhaṭ)}{झट (jhaṭ)}]{\mw{झट} (jhaṭ) — at once}

\label{lesson:MW-C167-jhat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for to sprinkle, then the Marwadi for last.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{झट}}
\textbf{\mw{झट}} — \emph{jhaṭ} — \textquotedblleft{}at once\textquotedblright{}.

\end{cousinweb}
